title: Pantry 7.0 weekly planner redesign
context: Pantry is a consumer meal-planning web app. 68% of sessions are on mobile (360-414px wide), and about 30% of users run the OS in dark mode, which the app has supported since v5. This proposal ships the redesigned weekly planner page to all web users on Tuesday.

defects.description: Below 768px the new action bar is position: fixed at the bottom with a 72px height, but .planner gets no bottom padding or safe-area inset. Sunday's card, the last child, is therefore permanently partly covered on mobile, where most sessions happen.

.day-card hardcodes a white background but takes its text color from var(--text), which becomes #f2f2f7 in dark mode. For about 30% of users the day cards render near-white text on white. QA only checked light mode.

The brief identifies adding a recipe to the shopping list as the most frequent planner action (9.4 times per week, mostly on mobile). The redesign removes the one-tap tile button and replaces it with a five-step path through the recipe page, the Ingredients tab and the servings sheet, adding friction to the core flow to declutter the tiles.
defects.evidence: The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles.

decoys: Drag-and-drop reordering is often inaccessible, but every tile has a 'Move to…' overflow-menu alternative, verified with keyboard and VoiceOver in QA.
Lazy-loaded images often cause layout shift, but the tiles set explicit width/height and Lighthouse reports CLS 0.01.
